dedupe_keys.name: heat risks at the world s top 100 data centre hubs maplecroft cooling degree days and water stress analysis

description: This Maplecroft analysis finds that rising global temperatures threaten the resilience of well over half of the world's top 100 data centre hubs, because higher cooling needs raise water and electricity demand, costs and the risk of conflict with local communities and power outages. It uses a Cooling Degree Days Index: 56 percent of the hubs currently score high or very high, rising to 68 percent by 2040 and 80 percent by 2080 under the SSP5-8.5 high-emissions scenario, with an average 83 percent increase in cooling degree days from 2030 to 2080; by 2040 all hubs in Asia-Pacific and the Middle East fall in the two highest categories, and in North America the share rises from 55 percent to 71 percent in 2040 and 90 percent in 2080. On water, 52 percent of hubs face high or very high water stress by 2030 and 58 percent by 2050, and an average mid-size data centre uses about 300,000 gallons a day. The article recalls that summer heat waves in the UK and US in 2022 forced some data centres offline. Producer: Maplecroft analysts including Laura Schwartz. Coverage: the world's top 100 hubs. Access: a public article with figures; the underlying indices are commercial products. Licence and cost: article free, data licensed. Caveats: index thresholds and the hub list are proprietary. Simulation uses: heat and water exposure benchmarks for siting and adaptation scenarios. Related record: XDI data centre physical climate risk 2025 (case_study-xdi-data-centre-physical-climate-risk-2025).
